domain: Looks up the active effect object (Data_02000240[125]) and derives its ground-grid X/Z tile from the integer half of its fixed-point x/z position. If a static one-shot flag is already set, resets the object (mode 10, teardown state) and clears the flag. Otherwise it computes the object's grid cell index into two parallel 128-wide tile-attribute tables (0x02010000 / 0x02010200) and aborts if their per-cell 'kind' bytes disagree or a placement probe (Func_08009220) rejects the position; on success it re-anchors the effect at the snapped tile, marks the flag active, and starts it moving toward the tile with an upward Y offset.

cross-edition=2026-08-30 correction: the comparator's zero Japanese row is the edition-delta baseline, not a candidate-versus-ROM exactness score. Permanent retention rests instead on the directly measured English evidence: complete semantics, exact 376-byte extent, equal topology, one localized reciprocal register-role family, bounded source experiments, and the allocator decoder/permuter verdict.

The listed family template (08092708, run_rising_sequence.c) supplied only the general object/WaitFrames/mode shape; the actual control flow, tile-snap arithmetic, and dual-table comparison were reconstructed directly from the assembly with no close template match.

Candidate matches the reference length exactly (376/376 bytes). The largest fix was branch polarity: the static-flag check must be written `if (flag == 0) { <large success path> } else { <reset path> }` -- the reverse ordering (testing `flag != 0` first) makes GCC place the reset path inline and the success path out-of-line, which is not what the reference does. A second fix was the tile-index arithmetic: it must be written as two sequential `if (x < 0) x = ...; x >>= 4;` guard statements (matching the assembly's fallthrough-then-shift shape) rather than a `(cond ? a : b) >> 4` ternary, which GCC compiles into extra out-of-line branches. A third fix corrected the struct's byte-offset layout (field_20 at 0x14, field_28 at 0x28, value_55 at 0x55, value_5a at 0x5a) after an initial padding-array miscount had them all landing 12-16 bytes too far into the struct.

Remaining differences are register/slot allocation only: which physical register the compiler assigns to grid_x vs. grid_z intermediates, the order it evaluates the two parallel-table pointers before their byte loads, and where exactly (relative to `mov fp,r1`) it schedules the `sub sp,#24` frame-reservation instruction (found by trial to require a 6-word stack array here even though only 3 words are read/written, which fixed the stack size but not this scheduling position). No further respellings tried moved these register/scheduling choices to match.

Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, the exact-C family template, and already-established local function signatures (Func_08092054, Func_080916b0, Func_080920e8, Func_080091e0, Func_08009080, Func_0809163c) from the wider source tree. No GS2 evidence or external source was used.

This did not reach zero.
measured=2026-08-29: Reversing grid_x/grid_z declaration order (grid_z before grid_x) regressed the score (differing_halfwords rose to 66); reverted.

measured=2026-08-29: Restructuring the two early-return failure sites (`if (kind mismatch) {Func_08091750(); return -1;}` and `if (result != 0) {Func_08091750(); return -1;}`) to share one `goto fail; ... fail: Func_08091750(); return -1;` tail (C89 goto/label) did not reproduce the reference's shared/merged tail or its trailing dead-code block; instead it changed candidate size to 380 bytes (vs. reference's 376) and topology to equal-but-`missing-extra-code`, with differing_halfwords rising to ~172-174. GCC 2.96 did not tail-merge the two call sites from this goto shape the way hypothesized, so shared-tail-via-goto is refuted as a way to reproduce the reference's dead trailing `bl;movs r0,#1;negs r0,r0` block. Reverted.

Note on environment: while iterating on this owner, the working copy of 08093e28.c was observed changing on disk between tool calls in ways this session did not perform (declaration order and duplicate/removed local declarations toggling, at least one instance of an unrelated `goto fail;` restructuring appearing and disappearing) -- a second concurrent agent/session was independently editing this same file. This made some incremental A/B comparisons noisy; every figure recorded in this dossier was re-verified against the file content actually on disk immediately before recording it.

measured=2026-08-29: Rewriting `s32 tile_x = TILE_HI(object,8) & 0xfff0; s32 tile_z = TILE_HI(object,16) & 0xfff0; s32 grid_x = 8+tile_x; s32 grid_z = 8+tile_z;` as `s32 grid_x = 8 + (TILE_HI(object,8) & 0xfff0); s32 grid_z = 8 + (TILE_HI(object,16) & 0xfff0); s32 tile_x = grid_x - 8; s32 tile_z = grid_z - 8;` (computing grid_x/grid_z directly and deriving tile_x/tile_z from them, instead of the reverse) fixed the `sub sp,#24` vs `mov fp,r1` prologue-scheduling divergence noted above (they now match exactly) and dropped differing_halfwords from 60 to 53, wrong_instructions from 34 to 24. This is the single largest improvement found this session. Kept.

measured=2026-08-29: Prior to the fix above, restructuring the kind-mismatch early return from `if (kind != kind2) { fail } else { <whole success block> }` to `if (kind == kind2) { <whole success block> } else { fail }` (flipping the polarity so the failure path is the trailing `else` of the outer `if`, mirroring the already-required flag-check polarity) dropped differing_halfwords from 113 to 60 on its own, before the grid_x/tile_x change above was applied. This is a second, independent required-polarity fix (distinct from the flag-check one already on record) and is kept.

measured=2026-08-29: With both of the above fixes applied, nesting the inner `if (result != 0) { fail }` early return as `if (result == 0) { <rest of success work> } else { fail }` (matching the same flip applied to the outer kind-check) is score-neutral (still differing_halfwords=53) but causes GCC to emit a second physical copy of the `Func_08091750(); return -1;` tail inline (visible as extra instructions right after the success path in the diff) rather than reference's single shared/merged copy reached by a long branch. The plain early-return form (`if (result != 0) { fail } <rest of success work continues>`) produces byte-for-byte identical output at the same differing_halfwords=53 without this duplication risk, so it was kept in preference to the nested form.

measured=2026-08-29: Converting the OUTER kind-check from if/else form back to a leading guard clause (`if (kind mismatch) { fail } { <success block, unindented> }`, i.e. guard-clause style instead of if/else-with-fail-in-else) regressed sharply to differing_halfwords=106. This confirms the outer kind-check specifically requires the if/else-with-fail-in-else polarity (guard-clause style is wrong here), unlike the inner result-check where either form scores the same. Reverted.

measured=2026-08-29: None of the following score-neutral (still 53) or regressing register-allocator nudges closed the remaining gap, all reverted: swapping grid_z/grid_x declaration order back after the fix above (regressed to 63); swapping tile_z/tile_x declaration order alone (regressed to 62-64 depending on combination); reordering `position[0..2]` assignment statements from x,y,z to z,y,x (regressed to 57); swapping the `Data_02010000`/`Data_02010200` operand order in the kind comparison (regressed to 55); writing `index = (index_z<<7)+index_x` instead of `index_x+(index_z<<7)` (regressed to 54); replacing `tile_x+23`/`tile_z+23` with algebraically-equivalent `grid_x+15`/`grid_z+15` (neutral, kept the tile_x/tile_z form for readability); moving the `s32 result;` declaration to various positions relative to `tile_x`/`tile_z`/`position` (neutral); extracting `Data_02010000[index].kind`/`Data_02010200[index].kind` into separate `u8 kind_a`/`kind_b` locals before comparing (regressed to 55). The remaining 53 differing halfwords are concentrated in one spot: which physical register (r2 vs r3) the compiler assigns to the `index_x` bounds-check/shift temporary right before it is stored to `sl` -- reference reuses r3 for both `index_x` and the later `index_z` processing, candidate uses a fresh r2 for `index_x`. This appears to be a GCC 2.96 local-register-allocator liveness/pressure artifact rather than something controllable from this statement's own source form; no respelling tried moved it. A downstream `bne.n` branch-offset difference (0x110 vs 0x106 in the flag check, and correspondingly 0x106 vs 0x14a in the two failure-path compares) is very likely a pure byte-offset consequence of this one register/instruction-count difference rather than an independent structural issue -- it was not separately pursued.

Cumulative result this session: differing_halfwords 113 -> 53 (53% reduction), wrong_instructions 36 -> 24, via two required if/else polarity fixes (outer kind-check, matching the already-known flag-check pattern) and one data-flow reordering fix (computing grid_x/grid_z first and deriving tile_x/tile_z from them, which also fixed the sub-sp/mov-fp prologue scheduling).
